design_rationale: Explicit 1:1 random allocation via computer-generated sequence in variable blocks, stratified by site, plurality and gestational age, administered by a third party: "Randomisation was performed by a computer-generated random allocation sequence in variable blocks of two, four and six."

domain_judgments.rationale: Computer-generated, third-party-managed, variable-block stratified sequence with concealed web-based allocation to pre-packed identical infusion bags, and baseline characteristics (Table 1) were closely comparable between arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Randomisation was performed by a computer-generated random allocation sequence in variable blocks of two, four and six. Randomisation was stratified by trial site, plurality and gestational age... The randomisation process was carried out by a third party (DEFACTUM, Central Region Denmark)... the attending obstetrician accessed a web-based program (Trialpartner) with a centre-specific log-on procedure. A trial number with a corresponding pre-packed set of infusion bags... was abstracted."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, caregivers and investigators were blinded with an identical-appearance placebo, adherence to the loading dose was high (95.3%) and balanced across arms, only two unblindings occurred (both retained in the analysis), and an intention-to-treat analysis was used; incomplete repeat loading dosing (53% of eligible) was due to staff error/emergency caesarean rather than knowledge of allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The infusion bags containing MgSO4 and placebo were identical in appearance. The participants, caregivers, and study coordinators at all sites, as well as the investigators were blinded to treatment assignment until all data were collected... The primary data analysis was performed for all enrolled patients on an intention-to-treat basis."

domain_judgments.rationale: Essentially complete ascertainment of the primary outcome — all surviving children in both arms had medical-record follow-up (100% and 100%, with ASQ in 100% vs 98.4%) — and all randomised fetuses/children were included in the primary ITT analysis, with similar follow-up duration in both arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "321 children survived until time of follow-up / 321 (100%) were followed-up through medical records ... 313 children survived until time of follow-up / 313 (100%) were followed-up through medical records / 308 (98.4%) were followed-up through medical records and Ages & Stages Questionnaire"

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcome (GMFCS-classified CP) is appropriate and assessors were blinded, and dual ascertainment (records plus ASQ) strengthens validity; however, extraction was performed by a single unblinded-to-identity investigator with no reported inter-rater reliability, and ascertainment intensity differed by gestational age at birth (routine paediatric follow-up only for those born <32 weeks), though this should be balanced across randomised arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "At follow-up, the medical records of all children were scrutinized by HTW for the diagnosis of CP and the GMFCS level... all parents were asked to complete the Ages and Stages Questionnaire (ASQ)... If the current gross motor skills were not age appropriate, the child was examined by an independent neuro-paediatrician for a possible CP diagnosis."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT01492608) with a pre-specified primary outcome and pre-specified analysis plan, but the sample size was downscaled mid-trial (1240 to 560) and secondary outcomes were added after initiation, so despite these changes being made before unblinding there remains some concern about selective reporting among the many secondary outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The planned statistical analyses were described before being carried out. ... After the initiation of the trial, but prior to unblinding, we added further secondary outcomes for the completeness of the data report."

overall_summary: This well-conducted double-blind, placebo-controlled multicentre RCT had robust concealed computer randomization, balanced baseline characteristics, effective blinding with an identical placebo, ITT analysis, and near-complete outcome ascertainment. Overall judgment is "some concerns" driven by single-rater outcome extraction with gestational-age-dependent ascertainment pathways (D4) and post-initiation addition of secondary outcomes plus mid-trial sample-size downscaling (D5), neither of which is likely to have substantially biased the pre-specified primary CP outcome.

design_rationale: Multicentre placebo-controlled trial in which 573 women were randomly assigned via computer-generated randomisation numbers (variable block size), stratified by centre, plurality and gestational age, with central telephone allocation ("Randomisation numbers were generated by computer using variable block size... Central telephone randomisation was managed by staff of the NICU at the Antoine-Béclère Hospital").

domain_judgments.rationale: Computer-generated stratified random sequence with variable block sizes and central telephone allocation ensured concealment; baseline characteristics were largely balanced, with only a modest PPROM imbalance consistent with chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Randomisation numbers were generated by computer using variable block size from 2 to 16... Central telephone randomisation was managed by staff of the NICU at the Antoine-Béclère Hospital, Clamart, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week."

domain_judgments.rationale: Women were blinded but treatment was only single-blind (anaesthetists/obstetricians aware of allocation, aided by characteristic flushes), so co-intervention/care differences cannot be excluded; however analysis was intention-to-treat and ~90% received the full dose, with a confirmatory per-protocol sensitivity analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Treatment assignment was single blind rather than double-blind... double blinding was deemed impossible to maintain for anaesthetists or obstetricians because MgSO4 infusion is usually responsible for characteristic flushes."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data to discharge were available for all randomised women and all 688 live fetuses retained; only 23 infants (3.3%) lacked CUS because they died very early (captured in the mortality/combined outcome), and 9 women from very low-recruiting centres were excluded under a predefined rule.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Outcome data were obtained until hospital discharge for all 564 women and 688 infants."

domain_judgments.rationale: Mortality is objective, and cranial ultrasound was read blind to allocation using prespecified lesion definitions, with a blinded central expert re-read of about half the infants showing substantial agreement (kappa 0.65) and essentially unchanged effect estimates.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "CUS was conducted by a senior neonatologist or radiologist in each centre separately and in a blind manner relative to treatment allocation."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial is registered (ISRCTN 00120588) with clearly prespecified primary outcomes, analysis plan and sample size, but recruitment was stopped early for non-statistical reasons at 62% of target and several adjusted/interaction and substitution analyses were presented post hoc without a publicly verifiable protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "When additional interaction terms between treatment group and PPROM or maternal–fetal infection were introduced, no significant improvements in the prediction of the primary outcomes were obtained, but more pronounced effects of MgSO4 were intimated."

overall_summary: Well-conducted, registered, placebo-controlled randomised trial with concealed computer-generated allocation, near-complete follow-up and blinded outcome assessment, but only single-blind treatment (clinicians aware of allocation) and post hoc adjusted/interaction analyses with early termination at 62% of target recruitment raise some concerns. Overall risk is therefore 'some concerns', driven by domains 2 and 5.

design_rationale: Explicit random allocation of pregnant individuals to magnesium sulfate or placebo via a central telephone randomization service with balanced variable block sizes and stratification, in a registered multicenter placebo-controlled trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Central telephone randomization with variable block sizes, stratification, schedule generated by an investigator not involved in clinical care (adequate concealment), and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Eligible pregnant individuals were randomly assigned to the magnesium group or the placebo group using a central telephone randomization service... The randomization schedule used balanced, variable block sizes and was performed by an investigator not involved in clinical care." / "The 2 groups were similar at trial entry (Table 1)."

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind placebo-controlled design with identical-appearing treatment packs, ~95% of participants received allocated treatment, and analyses followed a prespecified intention-to-treat approach; the high rate of recognizable magnesium side effects could partially unblind participants but is unlikely to affect objective outcomes such as death or blinded pediatrician-diagnosed cerebral palsy.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Participants, staff, investigators, and assessors of the children were blinded to the treatment allocation." / "Almost 95% of participants in each group received the allocated treatment" / "conducted following a prespecified statistical analysis plan with an intention-to-treat approach"

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 81% of infants (691/858 and 674/821) contributed to the pediatrician-assessed primary outcome (~19% missing), although missingness was balanced across groups, blinded assessment of missingness showed no concerning patterns, and a sensitivity analysis using all data sources (~96% coverage) gave similar results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Of the infants alive at trial entry, 691 of 858 (80.5%) in the magnesium group and 674 of 821 (82.1%) in the placebo group were included for the primary outcome... The complete case analysis was considered the primary analysis because the assessment of missing data, which was blinded to the treatment allocations, revealed no concerning patterns of missingness."

domain_judgments.rationale: Death is objective and cerebral palsy was diagnosed using standardized criteria (GMFCS, defined neurological examination) by pediatricians blinded to allocation, applied identically in both groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Participants, staff, investigators, and assessors of the children were blinded to the treatment allocation." / "A diagnosis of cerebral palsy required loss of motor function and abnormalities of muscle tone and power, with gross motor dysfunction classified using the Gross Motor Function Classification System"

domain_judgments.rationale: Trial was prospectively registered (ACTRN12611000491965) with published protocol and prespecified statistical analysis plan; the single prespecified primary outcome and prespecified sensitivity analysis are reported, with secondary outcomes explicitly labelled exploratory due to no multiplicity adjustment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "conducted following a prespecified statistical analysis plan with an intention-to-treat approach" / "No adjustment was made for multiple comparisons; thus, findings for the secondary outcomes should be interpreted as exploratory."

overall_summary: This well-conducted, registered, double-blind multicenter RCT had robust randomization, blinded and standardized outcome assessment, ITT analysis, and a prespecified analysis plan. The only limitation is ~19% missing data for the pediatrician-assessed primary outcome (balanced between groups and supported by a concordant sensitivity analysis), yielding an overall judgment of some concerns.

design_rationale: Explicit placebo-controlled randomized trial: "The study randomization numbers were generated by computer with variable block sizes of 4, 6, or 8" with stratification by center and multiple pregnancy, and women "randomly assigned" to magnesium sulfate or isotonic saline.

domain_judgments.rationale: Computer-generated, variable-block, centrally managed allocation concealed in identical masked treatment packs ensured concealment, and baseline characteristics were broadly similar with only minor imbalances (parity, race, hospital, patient status) consistent with chance and handled by adjusted analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The study randomization numbers were generated by computer with variable block sizes of 4, 6, or 8 and managed by nonclinical staff at the University of Adelaide's Maternal Perinatal Clinical Trials Unit. Each study number was placed on a masked treatment pack."

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding with identical placebo packs and a strict intention-to-treat analysis (including a sensitivity analysis) were used, but the markedly higher rate of recognizable minor adverse effects (89.0% vs 37.8%) and infusion discontinuation (14.6% vs 5.3%) in the magnesium group could have functionally unblinded women and attending clinicians and influenced co-interventions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "All statistical analyses were undertaken on an intention-to-treat basis, including outcome data from women who did not give birth preterm."; "The adverse effects led to the infusion being stopped only in a small percentage of women but more often in the magnesium sulfate group (78 [14.6%] vs 28 [5.3%])"

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 99% of 2-year survivors, with only 14 children (9 vs 5) lacking cerebral palsy assessments—an amount too small and too balanced to bias the effect estimates.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "2-year corrected age outcomes were available for 1047 children (99% of 2-year survivors). Fourteen children (9 in the magnesium sulfate group and 5 in the placebo group) without 2-year corrected age cerebral palsy assessments were treated as missing data"

domain_judgments.rationale: Mortality is objective, deaths were reviewed by a blinded independent committee, and 2-year neurodevelopmental assessments were conducted by developmental pediatricians and psychologists blinded to allocation using standard criteria; the acknowledged variability in cerebral palsy diagnosis across untrained assessors would be non-differential given blinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Surviving children were assessed at a corrected age of 2 years by developmental pediatricians and psychologists blinded to treatment group allocation."

domain_judgments.rationale: Pre-specified primary outcomes, sample size and analysis plan are clearly described and all were reported (all null), but no trial registration/protocol is cited and the headline conclusions rest on a secondary, multiply-tested outcome (substantial gross motor dysfunction) with no stated adjustment for multiplicity.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Substantial gross motor dysfunction (3.4% vs 6.6%; RR, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.29-0.91) and combined death or substantial gross motor dysfunction ... were significantly reduced in the magnesium group."

overall_summary: This large, well-conducted multicentre placebo-controlled trial had robust central randomization, near-complete 2-year follow-up and blinded outcome assessment, but raises some concerns because the distinctive side-effect profile of magnesium sulfate may have unblinded participants and clinicians, and because no protocol/registration is cited while the positive conclusions derive from secondary outcomes among many tested.

design_rationale: The MagNET Trial explicitly randomized consenting women in preterm labor to MgSO4, other tocolytic, or saline placebo using a computerized randomization program with stratified blocks of 6.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated, stratified sequence was used and the limited baseline table (race, gestational age, plurality) showed balance, but allocation concealment is never described, small fixed blocks of 6 in a partly open-label trial raise predictability concerns, and no broader baseline comparison (e.g., birth weight, PPROM) across arms is given.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "To ensure balance in the randomization process, a computerized program ... was used. Consenting women were randomized in stratified blocks of 6 on the basis of race (black versus other) and gestational age"

domain_judgments.rationale: The tocolytic arms were unblinded with the comparator left to clinician choice (only the preventive arms were "doubly masked"), and although an intention-to-treat analysis was performed, co-intervention/crossover (e.g., open-label MgSO4 exposure in non-magnesium arms, as suggested by magnesium exposure in some control cases in Table VI) is not quantified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "the women were randomized to treatment with either (1) MgSO4 ... or (2) other tocolytic therapy, according to the attending obstetrician’s choice among ritodrine, terbutaline, indomethacin, or nifedipine."

domain_judgments.rationale: The headline dose-response/regression findings rest on only 82 of 165 infants (50%), denominators vary widely across tables (e.g., 19/19 vs 107 for chorioamnionitis, 94 for interleukin-6), cerebral palsy follow-up completeness at 18 months is not reported, and no analysis addresses whether missingness was related to outcome or exposure.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Of 165 infants, 82 infants have both umbilical cord serum ionized magnesium levels and health outcome data available for analysis."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes (IVH graded by standard criteria, MRI-confirmed PVL, death, cerebral palsy) were objective or assessed by masked/consensus assessors using the same methods in all arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Final ultrasound diagnoses ... were made by consensus decisions of 2 pediatric radiologists. ... Diagnoses of cerebral palsy were made, or verified, by a developmental pediatrician ... The developmentalist was masked to the antenatal exposure variables."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was powered for IVH alone but reports a post hoc composite outcome, pooling of the two tandem trials, a median-split biomarker analysis, selective use of a 1-sided test despite stating all tests were 2-sided, and multiple bivariate/multivariable models with no protocol or pre-specified analysis plan available — strongly suggestive of selective reporting of favourable analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "These composite comparisons (32% [27/85 infants] vs 19% [15/80 infants]) approached statistical significance (odds ratio, 2.0; 95% CI, 0.99-4.1; 1-sided Fisher exact test, P = .04; 2-sided Fisher exact test, P = .07)."

overall_summary: Although randomization used a computerized stratified sequence and outcome assessors were largely masked, the key conclusions derive from post hoc composite outcomes, median-split biomarker analyses and regression models not pre-specified (including a selectively reported 1-sided P value), with cord magnesium/outcome data available for only half the infants. These high-risk judgments in the missing-data and selective-reporting domains, together with unblinded tocolytic arms, drive an overall high risk of bias.

design_rationale: Explicit random allocation: "Eligible, consenting women were randomly assigned in a double-blind fashion to receive either intravenous magnesium sulfate ... or identical-appearing placebo" with "Group assignment was made according to a computer-generated random sequence, with stratification according to clinical center."

domain_judgments.rationale: Computer-generated (urn) randomization stratified by center with identical-appearing placebo implies concealed allocation, and the extensive baseline table shows balance across 20+ characteristics (P>0.05 for all between-group comparisons), consistent with chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Group assignment was made according to a computer-generated random sequence,12 with stratification according to clinical center and, in twin pregnancies, weeks of gestation (<28 or ≥28)." ... "The baseline characteristics of the two groups were similar (Table 1)."

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind placebo-controlled design with high adherence, minimal off-protocol magnesium use, and an explicit intention-to-treat analysis; although adverse events (flushing/sweating in 65%/28% vs 6.6%/2.5%) could partially unblind participants and clinicians, the outcomes are objective child neurologic endpoints assessed years later and retreatment failures (staff error, urgent cesarean) were unlikely to be differential in a way that biases effect estimates.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The data from all patients were analyzed according to the group to which they were randomly assigned, regardless of whether they received the study medication." ... "Adherence to the assigned intervention was high, and off-protocol use of magnesium sulfate for tocolysis was infrequent (1.4%)."

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcome ascertained for 95.6% of fetuses with balanced loss between arms (1041/1096 vs 1095/1145) and no significant baseline differences among those lost, so bias from the small amount of missingness is unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Follow-up was achieved for 95.6% of the children." ... "The baseline characteristics of the women whose fetuses were lost to follow-up did not differ significantly between the two study groups."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome measures were appropriate and standardized (pre-specified CP criteria plus GMFCS grading, centrally read cranial ultrasounds, certified examiners), applied identically in both arms, in a double-blind trial with explicitly blinded adjudication of ambiguous cases.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "An annually certified pediatrician or pediatric neurologist made a diagnosis of cerebral palsy if two or more of the following three features were present..." ... "two pediatric neurologists who were unaware of the treatment assignment judged whether the children had moderate or severe cerebral palsy"

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered with a clearly pre-specified primary composite outcome, pre-specified secondary outcomes, a pre-planned sample size and group-sequential interim analysis plan, and the authors transparently label post hoc analyses as "nonprespecified" and explicitly caution that the favourable cerebral-palsy-alone finding is a secondary outcome that is "not statistically compelling."
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The primary outcome was the composite of stillbirth or infant death by 1 year of age or moderate or severe cerebral palsy, as assessed at or beyond 2 years of age" ... "(ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00014989.)" ... "We performed nonprespecified analyses that were stratified according to..."

overall_summary: All five RoB 2 domains were judged at low risk: a computer-generated, center-stratified randomization producing well-balanced groups; double-blind administration of identical-appearing placebo with high adherence and intention-to-treat analysis; 95.6% outcome ascertainment with balanced, non-differential loss; standardized, blinded, criteria-based diagnosis of cerebral palsy; and a registered protocol with a clearly pre-specified primary outcome and transparently labelled post hoc analyses. The only minor caveat (not sufficient to raise the judgment) is potential partial unblinding from magnesium's characteristic side effects, which is unlikely to influence objectively adjudicated child neurologic outcomes assessed 2 years later.
